summary: Iteration-12 verified the ranked queue-toast flicker fix end-to-end. Backend: 11/11 queue endpoint tests pass (join/status/leave/ack/bot-fill match found within window). Frontend Playwright: (1) Ranked SEARCHING toast stays continuously visible with a smooth 4Hz-driven 00:01 -> 00:13 timer and locked ETA (~00:27) — zero flicker over 12s. (2) MATCH FOUND flow verified with 100ms DOM sampling: match-found overlay appeared at 29338ms, 3->2->1 countdown ticked at 1000/2002ms, /play navigation occurred at 33572ms — 42 events captured in that ~4.2s window with 0 hidden-toast events. Toast persisted continuously through the entire countdown + 1.2s pre-nav delay. (3) Cancel Ranked -> toast tears down and does NOT ghost-reappear during a 15s watch. (4) Casual Quick Match cancel -> 120 post-cancel samples over 12s show 0 reappearance. All 4 regression scenarios pass; the layered fixes in QueueContext.jsx (15s cancel-guard on matched:true + delayed setQueueState(null) inside 1200ms setTimeout) do resolve the user-reported 'toast disappears and randomly pops back up' bug.
critical_code_review_comments: QueueContext.jsx has three separate cancel-guard bumps (15s at matched, 10s at cancelRanked, 6s at miss-teardown). All correct but the magic numbers should be centralised into named constants for readability.

QueueContext.jsx cancelRanked sets cancelGuardUntilRef to 10s but the request comment (line 68) says 10s and line 65 says 15s in the matched branch — comment vs code is consistent, just noting for future clarity.
server.py remains at ~8100 lines (well beyond 700-line guideline). Iteration-10 already flagged. Splitting recommended in a future cleanup pass; not blocking.
Backend has proper QUEUE_LOCK usage on GET/DELETE/POST + MATCHED_USERS 60s stale-sweep — no race conditions observed in end-to-end tests.
Frontend log during startup: three unauthenticated 401s on initial /api/auth/me before login (still cosmetic, flagged in iteration_11).
test_credentials: player1@shooter.com / player123 (from /app/memory/test_credentials.md). NOTE: mid-test we hit the 10-min ranked-leave penalty because Playwright disconnects before match end; had to unset ranked_ban_until directly in Mongo between runs.
seed_data_creation: None. To let ranked tests run cleanly I unset ranked_ban_until on player1 via MongoDB motor client (safe: just clears the ban field, doesn't touch stats). Command documented in context_for_next_testing_agent.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The ranked-leave penalty (10 min) auto-fires whenever a Playwright test disconnects mid-ranked-match. To re-run ranked-queue tests, first clear the ban: `cd /app/backend && python -c "import os,asyncio;from motor.motor_asyncio import AsyncIOMotorClient;from dotenv import load_dotenv;load_dotenv();c=AsyncIOMotorClient(os.environ['MONGO_URL']);asyncio.run(c[os.environ['DB_NAME']].users.update_one({'email':'player1@shooter.com'},{'$unset':{'ranked_ban_until':'','ranked_ban_reason':''}}))"`. Playwright pattern that reliably catches the match-found window: inject a setInterval(100ms) into the page BEFORE clicking ranked, sampling `document.querySelector('[data-testid="queue-match-found"]')` + `[data-testid="queue-toast"]` presence + `location.pathname`. Retrieve via `page.evaluate('() => window.__toastEvents')`. Direct Playwright `is_visible` polling at 250ms was too coarse to reliably catch the ~4.2s match-found window because of async batching. The 100ms setInterval pattern is bulletproof — captured 42 continuous events across the entire mf-to-nav window.
rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: user reported ranked queue toast 'disappears and randomly pops back up' after match found. Fix (already applied by main agent in QueueContext.jsx, verified here): (1) cancelGuardUntilRef.current = Date.now() + 15000 the moment matched:true arrives — this blocks the 3s background poll from re-invoking beginActivePoll during the 3-2-1 countdown + 1.2s nav-delay window. (2) The setQueueState(null) + related teardown moved INSIDE the 1200ms setTimeout that fires after the 3-2-1 countdown completes, so the 'Match Found!' overlay stays mounted until the browser actually navigates to /play (QueueOverlay's own location.pathname.startsWith('/play') guard then hides it). Verification: 100ms-resolution DOM sampling shows 42 consecutive events between match-found and /play nav, all with toast_present=true and match_found_present=true — zero flicker.
